[Monsheus] Ouch, I'm glad I had some backup saves. Playing through the game again would be a pain. Still, it would be better if the items in question triggered the achievement, instead of one-time only events.

[Monsheus] Btw, I recommend removing the chapter bosses achievements. We already get the Star Piece ones shortly afterwards.

[LupineDream] I'm speaking with admin about that.  It requires admin permission to demote the duplicates from core.  Added Alto Card  :)

[Monsheus] Oh, I didn't know about that. For the Alto Card achievement though, wouldn't it be better to add only the Soprano Card? We need the other 2 cards to get it anyway.

[LupineDream] Yeah, true...I'll think on that.  I haven't gotten to the stage of the game where you can.  But I've updated Wisdom and Alto Card.  If you turn in cricket pie now it should pop for you, i added alts

[Monsheus] Weird, I tried talking to Link many times and nothing, but it unlocked after I slept on the inn.

[LupineDream] Yea, its intended to trigger after a player sleeps at the inn and sees him (how you find him).  You can use that workaround if you have a save file already near completion.

[LiveFastCyYoung] Ugh. Started playing through this a couple weeks ago and now I see new achievements are being added. REALLY don't want to restart this. :(

[Olafur] hmmm, will you let us know when you feel like you've added all the achieves you're gonna add?

[infpgamer] I usually don't mind new cheevs added to a set but to RPG seems odd given how long they are.

[Alena] An idea would be to leave to add all the achievements together after the revision, since it is a rpg and there are events that do not repeat themselves.

[Monsheus] "First-Class Pirate" is broken.

[LupineDream] Fixed.  Whoops!  I'd typoed the condition freezing up the cheev.  It should pop now. (did for me on my save with all the treasures collected)  Give it a shot.

[Monsheus] Well, it still doesn't work for me. Can you give me a summary for what I need to do? Maybe I forgot something...

[LupineDream] Its the 4 rooms (flying koopa troopa cannonball, cannonball jump, 3 dimensional maze, coin chase), and then the 5th, which is the hidden barrel you knock off the stack, push over the switch then collect the map.  Collecting the map and item sets it.

[LupineDream] If you have discord, screen sharing your emulator to show exactly how you are performing it will help.  I can tell you either way, then, or if you send a video.

[Monsheus] It unlocked for me now, finally. There's still a problem though, it unlocked after I got 5 maps, not 6.

[LupineDream] Its been patched now.  For the rest of you, you can now obtain all 6 clues.  Thanks Lootimus Maximus for providing srm, GameDragon for a helpful tip, and Monsheus for reporting this

[Monsheus] Keep trying, it took me about 5 tries to get it.

English: This achievement is missable. 
Follow the tutorial for this achievement: after rescuing the princess from forced marriage, you will be sent back to the Mushroom Kingdom. 
There the princess will say that she will go to her room. After all the talk with the Chancellor, DO NOT LEAVE THE CASTLE (If you leave, the achievement will not unlock)! 
Inside the castle go to the princess' room. Inside the room, stand between the fireplace and the blue chair, facing the wall and press the A button. Done! The achievement will be unlocked :) 
Here's a video explaining: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m4npJNvaAlo

[cicco] Finally got it, when I first saw this minigame I thought it would be impossible for me to get all the coins but thanks to the video wedgordo posted I was able to better understand this minigame.

My first advice is to not give up on the run when you make a mistake but take this as a way to practice later parts of the course. Check your latency options, it may make timing the presses easier. Do not be afraid to take pauses, if you see that you are getting worse pause and do something else.

Waterfall section: the first thing you need to do is learning how to "swim" as other people said you can't swim more than 4 times otherwise you'll lose height but it's not necessary to always swim 3 times, you can also swim 1 or 2 times without losing too much height.
In my opinion the most difficult part of this section is getting the coins around the first cave, this is because there's little room for errors. On the right side of the cave, when going right from above DO NOT swim 3 times if you do you are going to be pushed into the cave. When you manage to get the coin to the right of the cave you have to lose as little height as possible because the last coin could despawn.

River section: this is easier than it seems, you don't have to memorize everything, it's a simple pattern.
You start on the upper lane, you immidiately switch to the lower lane, than you stay in that lane for two set of coins and switch to the upper, and then you repeat this pattern until the end. only when you are in the upper lane you have to take the coin right before switching lanes. So the pattern goes:
-Lower (5)
-Lower (4)
-Lower (4)
-Upper (4)
with the number in brackets representing the number of coins you have to take.
Be careful when switching lanes because you will have to immidiately jump at the right time to take the coin, it will take a bit of practice to learn the timing but it shouldn't be too difficult.

[Boobina] This cheevo isn't that bad, it just requires focus and knowing about arbitrary hitboxes.
I managed to do it first try after understanding what is wrong with the first cave and a good 15 minutes of practicing the barrels part.

About that first cave: There seems to be a hitbox issue, so you have to be as close as possible (3 frames above it I'd say) then quickly double tap right (Don't spam or you'll fall in the cave!) and you're fine. 
I believe that 1st cave avoiding is the hardest part of the whole minigame, simply because there seems to be an invisible wall northeast from it for some reason.
Rest of the "cataract" part is just easy honestly, just make yourself a route and stick to it. The only hiccup I noticed is that sometimes the coins south of the 2nd cave seem to disappear if you're too low so act accordingly and grab them from the side or above.

As for the barrel part, it's just muscle memory, so practicing with savestates is recommended until you're able to do it consistently.
Here's the pattern I noticed and noted on a piece of paper :

(^) X O O X
(^) X O O X
(^) X O O X
(^) X O O

That's the whole sequence (seems to be 4 repeats). It's long but easy to get used to once you separate it in those 4 sections like I did.

- (^) means there's a SINGULAR coin you have to grab before changing lane
- X means changing lane
- O means staying on the same lane

[Cassievania] Took me 6 tries. I didn't get it until I understood the mechanics of the minecart.

Imagine the minecart has 5 speeds.
- Your default speed is 3.
- Tapping or holding the brakes reduces your speed by 1.
- Surviving a hairpin turn requires speed 2.
- A mushroom sets your speed to 5.
- To survive a hairpin turn after using a mushroom, you need to TAP the brake button 3 times.
- As soon as your turning, you've survived the turn and can use a mushroom again.

OVERHEAD 1
1. Jump to get the mushroom and immediately use it.
2. Hold Right to get the next mushroom.
3. Brake at the tight turns, then use a mushroom as you're coming out of the final turn. Start braking just before the end of the straightaway.
4. Hold right to go onto the next mushroom path, then as you're approaching the turn before the mushrooms, use a mushroom and immediately jump twice out of the turn to get the mushrooms. Start braking at the end of the straightaway.
5. As you enter the stretch of track with a side-mushroom, use a mushroom (skipping the side-mushroom). Start braking once you see the track touching your track.
6. Jump to get a mushroom and use it once you land. Do it again, then brake once at the turn at the end. You should have 1 mushroom remaining and be at no more than 0:50:00.

SIDESCROLLER 1
1. You only need to press X and B here, so with one hand, mash X to constantly spend all your mushrooms to go as fast as possible.
2. Jump as soon as you get the first mushroom.
3. Jump as the bottom track disappears to get another mushroom.
4. Wait through a set of 5 coins. At the end of a set of 4 coins, wait half a second and then jump up a track, and then jump as soon as you land.
5. Fall to the bottom track and wait until you pick up 2 mushrooms.
6. Look at the top of the screen. Jump up a track once you see a mushroom at the top. Jump again when you collect a mushroom. Stop mashing X when you have 1 mushroom left. You should finish below 1:05:00.

source_title: Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars — RetroAchievements community comments
text:
[Cassievania] OVERHEAD 2
1. Immediately use a mushroom, jump, brake, jump, use mushroom, then when you're nearing the hairpin turn, brake twice. (X, B, Y, B, X... Y, Y.)
2. Wait a second to get to the track with a side-mushroom. Boost past it, then start braking near the end.
3. Brake for tiny track, then boost. Brake at the end.
4. Hold right to get onto the right track. Wait for the track with the mushroom and then boost. Brake at BOTH of the next 2 turns.
5. Hold left and then jump to take the shortcut. Don't boost, just brake once at the tight left+right turn. Don't boost here either.
6. Boost on the next turn, then start braking when you see the turn.
7. Don't do anything except jump to grab the mushroom. Then jump and boost once you reach the pothole. At the end of the track, jump to grab the mushroom and DON'T brake.
8. At the last of the 3 turns, boost, then brake twice well before the end of the track. If you're below 1:50:00, you've got it even if you miss a jump in the next section. If you're over 1:56:00, start over.

SIDESCROLLER 2
1. Just like Sidescroller 1, mash X to constantly spend all your mushrooms. This section is a series of hills and valleys.
2. Jump when you're 1 support beam before the bottom of the first 3 valleys to get 2 mushrooms. (You got the right spot of you get all 3 coins in the first valley.)
3. Jump at the coins near the top of the 3rd hill to grab the another mushroom.
4. Mash X to the end.

Esse é um troféu canalha!

Local: Yo'ster Isle

Antes de começar, eu recomendo que o Yoshi deve está pequeno.
Se não estiver, tudo bem, faça o teste com ele obeso.

1. Dê 15 cookies primeiro (Yoshi pequeno), depois mais 15 e saia pela saída sul, onde o Boshi está.
2. Volte salve o game na saída norte (onde o nosso Yoshi está), depois dê mais cookies ao Yoshi obeso, 18 agora, tudo de uma vez.

Ele pode dar três:

• Energizers;
• Crystallines;
• Bracers.

Se ele entregar qualquer um desses itens, da loading e dê o 18 cookies novamente.
O "Yoshi Ade" vai vir de forma aleatória.
Eu consegui na segunda vez, sendo um Bracers a primeira.

Pra conseguir cookies rapidamente é preciso vencer as corridas.
Não da pra confiar no Yoshi, então o esquema é esse.

2. Salve o game, depois fale com Boshi e escolha correr com o Yoshi.
Eu sei, é o inferno esse desafio mas você vai pegar o jeito e não vai perdeu mais nenhuma.
3. Ainda com Boshi, aposte 2 dos 3 cookies.
4. Na corrida, aperte os botões no CONTRATEMPO e NÃO NO RITMO da música.
5. Perto da linha de chegada use o cookie.

Depois de vencer, salve e volte a fazer tudo de novo, porém, sempre apostando os cookies mais alto do que antes, isso faz triplicar os ganhos.

[Zylosian] I got this one with pure luck, frustration, determination and hatred. No guide helped me much... All I know from doing my own crazy research is that the window between jumps is between 717- 850ish milliseconds. I got this time from recording my game footage and analyzing the time between jumps. You must push the button EXACTLY at the bottom most frame of the jump and you have about 3 frames to time it, every single press. 
Dunno if input lag is causing issues or if it's my own setup with my display. Most of the times my tries fall flat between 7-10 jumps. Getting the perfect timing is so precise it's maddening. If I could get the exact BPM I'd use a bloody metronome, which is around 73ish BMP but even that feels off. I feel like I'm going crazy trying to aim for the 100 jumps. Least I got the 30 though... Ha ha... ha...

[SteelCat] The trick I found is that before 14 jumps, the "extra frames" on the timing window are from the START of the window, not the end. So while on jumps 1-13 it is way more forgiving of early hits, it is still just as unforgiving of late hits as 14+, so to find the window for 14+ you need to try and be as late as possible on jumps 1-13 and find out exactly the point where it registers as an obvious late input (easier to see during 1-13 because the early window is more forgiving). On earlier jumps, you will FEEL when you are late, try to hone in on exactly when that happens.

Then make a note of where Mario's sprite is exactly just before that point, and time your hits to that sprite placement. Online guides that show visuals for this timing are not useful, as they're either using original hardware or an emulation setup that is different than yours, you gotta find your own timing AND a cue to make it consistent.

[Mia] Just chiming in here to reinforce that if you can regularly get past the 13th jump then you CAN get this achievement. It will most likely take a bit of grinding and a lot of focus, but you can do it. 

I tried practicing on multiple enemies (goomba, spikey, artichoker)and what worked best for me is getting a group of 3 goombas in Mushroom Way and super jumping on the middle goomba because it is the lowest on the screen. I watched for Mario's right foot and when it was in the goomba's face thats when I pressed the button. Goombas were easiest for me because of this tell. Enemies that don't move are supposedly best but things like Artichoker have a hard tell of when Mario is actually landing on them.

Recommend getting the EarlierTimes item in Seaside Town via frog coins to make this grind a lot more bearable. What it does is reset the fight including any enemies you killed and FP you used, so it really helps on not having to find another trio of goombas or going back to heal FP. Also having a party where Mario goes first (Mario, Bowser, Mallow) to save you having to defend with an ally is really nice. All these little things add up in saving a lot of time in the long grind.

Worth noting that I got it 3rd try on a fresh morning, so if you're feeling burnt out on grinding maybe it's best to take a break and come back later. Good luck!!!

[HydroBobOmb] I just got it. Thanks to TindalosKeeper who said the rhythm of the jumps is at 80 BPM, I used a metronome and I noticed one thing : the jumps are indeed around this beat, but the time Mario spend to starting the super jump seems to be around one beat AND A HALF. The problem is how to start from a good point.

So, I used a metronome of 160 BPM and I tried to start the super jump on this beat. If did correctly, Mario will be pretty much aligned on the beat when bouncing on the enemy and reaching the peak of his jump.
It was very helpful for me. To have an audio cue is good instead of focusing purely on a visual cue, which is pretty tiring (just blinking my eyes screwed me a lot). 

Maybe using a 160 BPM metronome can help you too. The thing is to have a good cue of when you are at the middle frame of the 3 frames window. There is no strict setup to align the beat on this specific frame, but if you got it, it can carry you and save your energy (like avoiding to stare at one point of the screen).

[cicco] Finally did it after a week of grinding, don't give up you can do it.
If you can't do more than 13 jump try checking your latency settings, this helped me immensely.

It took me a lot of practice to do this so what I did to minimize the time loss was to grab a bunch of royal syrup and jump on a spikey without jump shoes equiped so that I would do 0 damage and i could stay in battle as long as I wanted. You don't need to count how many jumps you do since the game will prevent you from doing more than 100 so you just need to go for as long as you can focusing on the timing only. If you can do more than 13 jumps it means you are on the right path and you just need to grind more. The longer you grind the more you get used to the timing and you will start to feel the weight of each jump less and less, today's 40 jumps will feel like yesterday's 30 jumps and tomorrow's 50 jumps will feel like today's 40.

I used both a visual and an audio cue that worked for me, now this might not work for you but I'll explain so you can test if it works.
-As a visual cue I looked below the spikey's right eye, that area is where you will see mario's left foot at its lowest, what worked for me was pressing the button when i saw mario's foot.
-As an audio cue when the 1-up sound plays you have to press the button just after the first note, this is what worked for me, it took me a long time to get used to this but after you get used to it you can use it as a sort of metronome.

You will get tired grinding for this so you need to take pauses for as long as you need, what I noticed is that I was more performing in the first few attempts than the later.

Good luck with these achievement, keep on grinding and don't give up, you can do it.

------SUPER MARIO RPG: LEGEND OF THE SEVEN STARS FAQ/WALKTHROUGH-------
------Written by NickWhiz1 (NickWhiz1@buckeye-express.com)-------------
------Version FINAL----------------------------------------------------
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Last Updated: April 15, 2002
Happy Tax Day Everyone!

Table of Contents:

1. Introduction/History

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. INTRODUCTION/HISTORY----------------------------------------------------
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

4/15/02: Fixed up section dividers.

Version FINAL(2/27/02): Finished up the last couple sections.  I'm finally done
with my second longest guide!

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Who do you think wrote this? :P

 Who do you think is reading this? :P

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. STORY-------------------------------------------------------------------
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Note: A dead stick could come up with a better storyline in the first couple
stages, but the rest is quite interesting.

One day we see Princess Toadstool sitting outside Mario's house looking at
flowers, alone (here it comes!).  Suddenly, the sky goes back and our favorite
Mario villain snatches her away (I won't tell who, because it's so obvious).
Anyways, Mario goes into Bowser's Keep and, well, you know the rest.

Just before Mario unties the Princess, the keep starts shaking.  The camera
goes outside just in time to see a giant sword bust through the "Star Road"
(explained later) and crashes into the keep, knocking the inhabitants out.  We
then see the seven broken star pieces fall to the ground, the 7th one dropping
down onto the sword just as the screen begins to fade away...

After crash landing back at his house and listening to Toad, Mario heads back
to the keep to rescue Princess Toadstool.  While he's standing on the bridge
between the keep and Vista Hill, he sees the sword for the first time.  The
sword explains about the "Smithy Gang" and their plans to take over the world.
He then breaks the bridge and the keep is unaccessable, until later.

The main object of the game is to work your way through the levels, defeat the
members of the "Smithy Gang", and collect the seven star pieces.  He will not
go alone, though.  He will be joined by a prince-who-thinks-he's-a-tadpole, a
mysterious spirit from the Star Road disguised as a doll, and two "mystery
characters".  (Hint: Villains and damsels-in-distress make good companions,
sometimes.  Or, you could just read the "Characters" section.)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. CONTROLS----------------------------------------------------------------
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Normal:

Control Pad: Move around, move cursor
A Button: Talk to someone, check something out, accept on a menu
B Button: Jump, cancel on a menu
X Button: Go to the menu screen
Y Button: Hold to walk faster
L and R Buttons: Switch between Stereo and Mono at the beginning of the game
Select Button: Switch between Stereo and Mono at the beginning of the game
Start Button: Starts game

In Battle:

Control Pad: Choose target, scroll through special moves, items, and Etc.
options
A Button: Attack mode, select target
B Button: Etc. mode, select either Defense or Run Away
X Button: Item mode, select item
Y Button: Special mode, select special technique, select target

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. ITEMS-------------------------------------------------------------------
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

This section contains information on items, as well as weapons, armor, and
accessories.

===========================================================================
ITEMS
===========================================================================

Choosing items to keep in your inventory is hard, especially since you can only
29 at a time.  Here is a list showing all of the items.

ABLE JUICE
*Affects: 1 Ally
*Use: Battle only
*Effect: Restores status to normal

6. CHARACTERS--------------------------------------------------------------

===========================================================================
MARIO
===========================================================================

Who in a million years would even imagine Mario would star in an RPG?  Not me.
Anyways, Mario comes in with his traditional hammers, fire, and jumps.  You
start out the game with him.

*TIMED ATTACKS*
Punches: Press the A button just before he punches.
Hammers: Press the A button really close to when he makes impact with the first
swing.
Shells: Press the A button right after the shell comes down so Mario can kick
it at the enemy.

*SPECIAL ATTACKS*
-JUMP-
*Level Learned: Mario begins with it.
*FP Used: 3
*MP Rating: 25
*Classification: Jump
*Description: Stomp foes!  Push "Y" just before hit!
*My Comments: Jump is very useful early in the game.  Learn how to time it, as
you can do major damage while applying the timing with Super and Ultra Jumps.

-FIRE ORB-
*Level Learned: Mario learns it at Level 3.
*FP Used: 5
*MP Rating: 20
*Classification: Fire
*Description: Fire orb!  Push "Y" repeatedly!
*My Comments: This is Mario's basic fire attack.  Learn how to press the Y
button quickly, as the Super and Ultra Flames will do tons of damage with
multiple hits.

-SUPER JUMP-
*Level Learned: Mario learns it at Level 6.
*FP Used: 7
*MP Rating: 45
*Classification: Jump
*Description: Push "Y" prior to hit for DAMAGE!
*My Comments: This is an advanced form of the Jump.  If you time it
correctly, Mario will bounce off the enemy and begin another jump attack.  Keep
timing it and Mario will keep jumping.  If you do 30 or 100, you can get items.
 The timing changes every few jumps, so pay attention.

-SUPER FLAME-
*Level Learned: Mario learns it at Level 10.
*FP Used: 9
*MP Rating: 40
*Classification: Fire
*Description: Fire blast!  Push "Y" repeatedly!
*My Comments: This attack deserves a higher MP rating then the Super Jump.
Performed correctly, and this will certainly unleash a lot of damage on
unsuspecting opponents.  Any enemies weak against Fire are in for a lot of
trouble!

-ULTRA JUMP-
*Level Learned: Mario learns it at Level 14.
*FP Used: 11
*MP Rating: 65
*Classification: Jump
*Description: Push "Y" prior to hit for DAMAGE!
*My Comments: This atacks has the highest MP rating!  It is very similar to the
Super Jump, except this time Mario can jump off one enemy and onto another!
The enemies he attacks and in what order are always random, but it is very
useful in a room full of weak-to-jump enemies (try using it on the Heavy
Troopas in Nimbus Land!).

-ULTRA FLAME-
*Level Learned: Mario learns it at Level 18.
*FP Used: 14
*MP Rating: 60
*Classification: Fire
*Description: Fire orbs!  Press "Y" repeatedly!
*My Comments: As with the Ultra Jump, this attack randomly hits more than one
enemy on the screen.  If you ever get to Level 18 on the Sunken Ship, use it to
make fried squid (as in, King Calamari squid!).

===========================================================================
MALLOW
===========================================================================

Only 2 people know exactly who Mallow is, and they are his parents.  To find
his parents, he decided to travel along with Mario, at Frogfucius's request.
His true past helps foil one villain's plan in Nimbus Land.  Mallow joins you
in Mushroom Kingdom when you agree to help him chase Croco.

*TIMED ATTACKS*
Punches: Press the A button just before he punches.
Sticks: Press the A button just before the stick hits the enemy.
Cymbals: Press the A button just before the attack is over.

*SPECIAL ATTACKS*
-THUNDERBOLT-
*Level Learned: Mallow begins with it.
*FP Used: 2
*MP Rating: 15
*Classification: Thunder
*Description: Hit "Y" just before bolt ends!
*My Comments: This is a very potent attack early on, and in a few cases later
on.  Just for this and other attacks, Mallow should always be in your party,
except in some boss battles.

-HP RAIN-
*Level Learned: Mallow learns it at Level 3.
*FP Used: 2
*MP Rating: 10
*Classification: N/A
*Description: HP renewal!  Hit "Y" just before shower ends!
*My Comments: Until Toadstool joins you, this is the only HP-recovering special
attack.  Actually, not very useful, unless you're out of Mushrooms and you have
a few extra FP to burn.

-PSYCHOPATH-
*Level Learned: Mallow learns it at Level 6.
*FP Used: 1
*MP Rating: N/A
*Classification: N/A
*Description: See foe's HP and... secrets!
*My Comments: For 1 FP to see inside an enemy's mind, this is a bargain.  To
time, press Y just before the two spotlights converge.  The message given
sometimes gives a hint on what attack to use, or they're just plain silly.

-SHOCKER-
*Level Learned: Mallow learns it at Level 10.
*FP Used: 8
*MP Rating: 60
*Classification: Thunder
*Description: Hit "Y" just before bolt ends!
*My Comments: Imagine Mallow's Thunderbolt attack contained into one giant bolt
and focused on just 1 enemy.  Use this attack, and see if it's what you
imagined.  This is EXTREMELY useful in the later stgaes, especially within the
battle with Culex...

-SNOWY-
*Level Learned: Mallow learns it at Level 14.
*FP Used: 12
*MP Rating: 40
*Classification: Ice
*Description: Snowman fells foes!
*My Comments: This must be the longest attack in the game (besides Geno Flash).
 Anyways, it creates a blizzard, then a giant snowman drops on the enemies and
disappears.  Very useful in the Barrel Volcano.

-STAR RAIN-
*Level Learned: Mallow learns it at Level 18.
*FP Used: 14
*MP Rating: 55
*Classification: N/A
*Description: Star showers!  Hit "Y" just upon contact!
*My Comments: I don't use this very often, because is hard to do and doesn't do
too much damage.  The timing is similar to the Super Jump.  If you want a good
multi-enemy attack, use the Geno Blast or Geno Flash.  Don't waste 14 FP on
this.

===========================================================================
GENO
===========================================================================

If you're a big fan of magic attacks, this is your guy.  His real name is
really hard to pronounce, so he took the name of Geno, from the doll.  You see,
he's from the Star Road, and since he's a spirit, he took the form of the doll
by breathing life into it.  He offically joins your party after you save him
from Bowyer.

*TIMED ATTACKS*
Punches: Press the A button just before he punches.
Guns: Press the A button just before he shoots.

*SPECIAL ATTACKS*
-GENO BEAM-
*Level Learned: Geno begins with it.
*FP Used: 3
*MP Rating: 40
*Classification: N/A
*Description: Hold "Y" until just before discharge!
*My Comments: Since none of Geno's attacks (which all start with Geno) have a
classification, they work on all enemies.  That's a good thing.  Only use this
when there's one enemy on screen.

-GENO BOOST-
*Level Learned: Geno learns it at Level 8.
*FP Used: 4
*MP Rating: N/A
*Classification: N/A
*Description: Attack up!  Push "Y" just before end!
*My Comments: I almost NEVER use this attack.  In fact, I almost never use
Bracer, Energizer or any other of those items.  But, this is actually a very
good attack to use.

-GENO WHIRL-
*Level Learned: Geno learns it at Level 11.
*FP Used: 8
*MP Rating: 45
*Classification: N/A
*Description: Press "Y" prior to contact for critical hit!
*My Comments: Unless you can time it right, this is totally useless.  But, if
you time it right, it does 9999 damage (instant death!).  It doesn't work on
stronger enemies or all bosses, though.

-GENO BLAST-
*Level Learned: Geno learns it at Level 14.
*FP Used: 12
*MP Rating: 50
*Classification: N/A
*Description: Beam hits all foes!  Energize!
*My Comments: This is the best multi-enemy attack until you get Geno Flash.
For only 12 FP and a three star charge-up, this is one very potent attack to
use.  Especially works when you're up against 4 or more enemies (6 is the max).

-GENO FLASH-
*Level Learned: Geno learns it at Level 17.
*FP Used: 16
*MP Rating: 60
*Classification: N/A
*Description: Build power!  Beam hits all foes!
*My Comments: THE BEST MULTI-ENEMY ATTACK IN THE GAME!  Once you have this, the
Geno Blast is obsolete, except when you have less than 16 FP.  This is most
effective against 4-6 enemies, just like the Geno Blast.  And yes, all of his
special attacks begin with his name, so bummer.

To quote the Chancellor: "WHAT'S GOING ON HERE?"  That's a perfect way to sum

===========================================================================
Q: I've heard of invisible treasure boxes.  Where are they?
===========================================================================

A: There are invisible treasure boxes scattered throughout the game, 39 to be
exact.  Here is a complete list of locations for each one.

---MUSHROOM KINGDOM---
1)(Frog Coin) You can only perform this if it's on your first visit, after
defeating the Hammer Brothers.  When you enter the castle, Toad will begin
walking down the hallway.  Jump on his head and jump to the ledge above the
door.

2)(Flower) Go into the item shop, and downstairs to the basement.  Talk to the
guy and follow his directions.  It's right above where he originally stood.

3)(Flower) You must be patient for this one.  After getting the previous one,
jump on his head and wait until he walks to the far-right corner, then jump.
This might take a while.

---BANDIT'S WAY---
4)(Kerokero Cola) Remember the second spinning flower in the 2nd area?  Jump on
it, then jump off, aiming for the purple flower, or just jump off straight
right.  You'll hit it at the top of your jump.

---ROSE TOWN---
5)(Frog Coin) Go into the item shop, and jump onto the bookshelf behind the
shopkeepers.  It is at the furthest left extent of it.

6)(Frog Coin) Hop on the guy's head near the house-on-a-hill to get up there.
Go inside, and go up to the 2nd floor.  It is located right above the bed.

---FOREST MAZE---
7)(Kerokero Cola) As soon as you enter, go to the far left corner.  It'll be
right there.

8)(Frog Coin) After you exit the first cave, go to the far left corner.  It
should be there.

9)(Flower) In the room with 7 stumps, jump into the furthest right one.  It is
right above the patch of light in the middle of the room.

10)(Empty!) In the room with 7 stumps, going from the entrance to the room,
enter the left stump in the 2nd row.  It's in the corner behind the trampoline.
 There's NOTHING inside! HAHAHAHAHAHAHA (sorry!)

11)(Kerokero Cola) In the room with 7 stumps, go into the far back one.  After
you wake up thr Wiggler and you come flying out, go back in and it's right
above where the Wiggler was.

12)(Red Essence) In the room with the Save Block, go into the far right corner.
 This forest is full of secret items!

---PIPE VAULT---
13)(Frog Coin) In the room with 6 pipes, go down the second one from the left.
Go one space left of the end of the higher ledge and jump to reveal a platform.
 It's around the 2nd or 3rd block.

14)(Frog Coin) In the same room, it's about 2 or 3 blocks right of the previous
one.

---YO'STER ISLE---
15)(Frog Coin) After you emerge from the pipe exit of the Pipe Vault, jump
behind the Save Block and you will find it.

---BOOSTER PASS---
16)(Flower) Go to the far left part of the first area and jump onto the flower.
It's right above there.

17)(Rock Candy) Just before the exit to the first area, go into the small
alcove just to the left of it.

---BOOSTER TOWER---
18)(Frog Coin) In the room with the eternal line of Spookums, go to the
furthest right dark block on the back wall, about where they turn and go down
the staircase.

19)(Frog Coin) In the room right above the Thwomp teeter-totter, go to the far
left corner on the lowest level.

section: Q: I've heard of invisible treasure boxes. Where are they?
text:
20)(Goodie Bag) In the room just before the curtain game room, jump up the
yelloe blocks onto the visible one.  It's right above it.

21)(Mushroom) In the same room, go to the corner directly next to the right
exit.  This one restores all HP AND FP.

---MARRYMORE---
22)(Frog Coin) Walk into the inn/item shop and go up to the 2nd floor.  Enetr
the normal room and jump onto the bookshelf in the far left corner.

---SUNKEN SHIP---
23)(Kerokero Cola) This one is interesting.  In the room with the Mario clone,
you have to make a block appear to show the treasure box, then you must jump
onto the clone's head to get up to it.

---LAND'S END---
24)(Red Essence) In the first room, use the cannon to shoot onto the moving
platforms.  You will need to jump STRAIGHT forward(/\) at the exact top of the
platform's ascent to get it.

25)(Kerokero Cola) In the second room, jump between the cannon and the plateau
to find a hidden platform.  Use the cannon to shoot into the hole with the
three Chows.  After defeating them, get on the left side of the hole, near the
higher plateau, and jump around for another platform.  Get back in the cannon
and shoot to the new platform.  After getting the moving treasure box, jump
onto the higher plateau and go to the far left side.  Sorry this description
was so long, but it takes a while to reach.

26)(Frog Coin) In the room with spinning flowers and Stingers, go to the two
purple flowers on the far right part of the room, jump on one of them, and jump
to the other.  You should get it.

27)(Frog Coin) Enter the cave below the Sky Bridge.  After passing the Chow, go
into the furthest back corner.  You might need to search, as it is hard to
explain this one.

---BELOME'S TEMPLE---
28)(Frog Coin) In the room after your first fortune is fulfilled, jump on the
higher ledges and jump on top of the visible treasure box on the left.  It's
right above it.

29)(Frog Coin) In the same room, go down the stairs and go into the alcove
directly right of it.

---MONSTRO TOWN---
30)(Frog Coin) In the room just before the exit, jump into the space between
the corner and the bush.

---BEAN VALLEY---
31)(Rock Candy) When you enter, go into the right pipe, and you'll find it in
the far left corner.

32)(Kerokero Cola) In the room with 5 Piranha Plants in pipes, go into the
lower right one and it'll be near the far left corner.

33)(Red Essence) In the room with 5 Piranha Plants in pipes, go into the far
right one and it's in the corner halfway between the trampoline and those
stairs.

---NIMBUS LAND---
34)(Frog Coin) Go into the item shop, jump onto the highest point of the
crates, and jump towards the shopkeeper.

35)(Frog Coin) Go to the hallway with the three doors, and go into the left
door.  Work your way to the Jawful, defeat it, and it'll be right above where
you found it.

36)(Frog Coin) In the same room as the last one, walk directly left to walk out
into space, and it'll be at the end of the path.

37)(Frog Coin) After you beat Birdo, go to the next room, with the Jawful.
Jump on top of the visible box.  It's right above it.

38)(Frog Coin) After defeating Valentina, go to the hallway with the three
doors, and go to the right of the birdcage next to the left door.

---SMITHY FACTORY---
39)(Mushroom) In the room with the second Save Block, go to the corner directly
left of the block.  That's the last one.

If you ever want to know how many boxes you missed, talk to the Pandorite in
Monstro Town.  Since I haven't actually gathered all 39 on one file (although I
have found all of them), I don't know what happens, but I think you don't get
anything for gathering all 39, except personal satisfaction and all of the
items inside the boxes.  It's fun to try to get all 39, but it's not that hard
once you know where they are.  This is an easier challenge than trying to get
30 or 100 Super Jumps, and a whole lot more possible.  I think you should get
something for finding all 39.  If you're having problems figuring out which
rooms they are in, equip the Signal Ring from Croco to find the correct rooms.

section: Q: How do I work out the Menu (pause) screen?
text:
===========================================================================
Q: How do I work out the Menu (pause) screen?
===========================================================================

A: Press the X button while on the normal screen to bring it up.  Here is a
chart showing the controls:


            |--------<X or B twice<--------|
            |-<X or B<-|         |<--B<----|
Normal Screen          Menu Screen         Menu Option
            |---->X>---|         |--->A>---|

These are the options available via the menu screen:

*Item: Check your inventory and/or use one or more items.
*Status: See your stats, experience, and how much more experience is needed to
go to the next level.
*Special: See your special attacks, and/or use Mallow's HP Rain or Toadstool's
Therapy or Group Hug.
*Equip: Equip and take off weapons, armor, and accessories.
*Special Item: See your inventory of special items.
*Map (get from Chancellor): See the world map and where you are on it.
*Star Pieces (after defeating Mack): See how many star pieces you have.
*Switch (after Bowser joins): Switch allies available for battle.
*Game (buy Beetle Mania in Mushroom Kingdom, see Mini-Games) Select if you wish
to play Beetle Mania.

section: Q: Could you give a detailed explanation about battles?
text:
===========================================================================
Q: Could you give a detailed explanation about battles?
===========================================================================

A: Here's my special section about battles:

---COMMANDS---

A Button: Attack: This one you will probably be using most of the time.  Press
A once to see what weapon you have and to pick a target.  Press A again to
attack.  To time it, press the A button at the time the different weapons
specify (see Timed Attacks under each character).

B Button: Etc.: There are two commands under this one.  If you choose Defense,
your character will shield themselves and cut damage by 1/2 (if you do a timed
block here also, it'll be cut by 3/4!).  If you choose Run Away, that's exactly
what will happen.  Sometimes you can't run away because the option is
deactivated, one of your characters has a status problem, or the game just
won't let you.

X Button: Item: Choose which item you want to use.  Press X once to se your
inventory.  Choose an item and press X to decide who to use it on, then press
it again to use it.  Sometimes you'll get "a freebie".  It either occurs
randomly, or maybe you time it like your attack and defense...

Y Button: Special: Don't use this one too often, unless you have plenty of FP.
Press Y once to choose an available attack (unavailable if not learned, not
enough FP, or no use for like Toadstool's Come Back).  Press Y again to decide
who to use it on, then press Y again to commence the attack.  Use the specific
directions for each attack to pull them off right.

---STATUS---

I know, you've heard me talk about status so much, but you're probably
wondering what it is.  Well, status is what condition your characters are in.
There are 7 different kinds of status:

*Normal: All commands available, no effects
*Fear: All commands available, all stats cut in half
*Poison: All commands available, HP taken off each battle turn (figured out by
taking your HP, dividing it by 10, and the decimals are cut off without
rounding)
*Sleep: No commands available, vulnerable to attacks, wake up after normal
attack or out of HP
*Silence: Special command not available, no other effects
*Scarecrow: Attack and item commands not available, no other effects
*Mushroom: No commands available, HP regained each battle turn (same system as
poison).

The non-normal ones can be healed with a Able Juice, Freshen Up, or Toadstool's
Therapy and Group Hug attacks.

---DISPLAY---

The way the screen is displayed is like this:


  HP of 3rd Charatcer
 HP of 2nd Charatcer
HP of 1st Character
                                                        Enemies


   1st Character (always Mario)

          2nd Character (once Geno is gained)

                3rd Character (once Geno is gained)/
                2nd Character (if just Mario and Mallow)

I know, I could've done better, but this is a hard one to do!

---SPECIAL ATTACKS---

Some enemies have special defenses against certain attacks (A.K.A. 0 Damage
taken) or weaknesses (A.K.A. tons and tons of damage).  The attacks are divided
into 9 classifications (8 really, but I added N/A as Normal).  The special
attacks AND items are listed next to each category.

N/A or Normal: Any special attack or item not in the next 8
Jump: Jump, Super Jump, Ultra Jump
Fire: Fire Orb, Super Flame, Ultra Flame, Fire Bomb
Thunder: Thunderbolt, Shocker
Ice: Snowy, Ice Bomb
Fear: Terrorize, Fright Bomb
Poison: Poison Gas, Bad Mushroom
Sleep: Sleepy Time, Sleepy Bomb
Silence: Mute

section: Q: When I go up a level, which bonus should I pick?

text:
===========================================================================
BOWSER'S KEEP
===========================================================================

-They should come up with a harder starting level.  Anyways, this visit is
comprised of four rooms:
Room #1: Basically, the welcoming room.  Nothing to worry about.
Room #2: A group of Terrapins guard this hallway.  If you go into battle, just
do any attack and they'll go away.  Before you get to the door, you'll go into
battle with 4 Terrapins.  Piece of cake.
Room #3: There are two bridges in this room going over the lava.  Just go up to
the door.  Before you enter the door, Bowser will roar and the bridge right
behind you will collapse.  Who would want to go back anyways?
Room #4: The chandalier room.  Walk up to the far side of the room and you'll

section: see two chandaliers, with Bowser on one of them. Battle time...
text:
see two chandaliers, with Bowser on one of them.  Battle time...
===========================================================================
BOSS: Bowser
-Bowser: N/A
-Kinklink: N/A
HP: 0/50
Defenses: Bowser: N/A
          Kinklink: N/A
Weaknesses: Bowser: N/A
            Kinklink: N/A

This is a very easy battle to win.  All you have to do is aim for the Kinklink.
 It will take two timed Jumps or three timed punches to end the battle.
===========================================================================
-After trampling Bowser, you'll see Mario up on a Kinklink, about to untie
Toadstool, being tied from the ceiling.  Just before it happens, the castle
will shake.  Moving outside, you'll see a sword come through the sky (wait, I'm
retelling the story).

===========================================================================
MARIO'S PAD
===========================================================================

-Ah, Mario's humble pipehouse.  The giant pipe up there, what can it be used
for?  Let's find out, shall we?
-At first, you'll see Toad standing outside, waiting for Mario, then he'll see
Mario come flying and go through that oversized pipe atop his house.  Toad the
comes in, and says something about people normally use doors to get in and out
of their houses, then go outside.  Go talk to him, and he'll suggest you go
back to Bowser's Keep to rescue the Princess.  Save your game here, then go to
Bowser's Keep again.

===========================================================================
BOWSER'S KEEP
===========================================================================

-Rule #1: If a giant sword is about to destroy the bridge you're on, run
straight for the other side.  Rule #2: Omit Rule #1 if Toadstool isn't inside.
Anyways, after the sword talks about the Smithy Gang's plans for world
domination, he'll shake and break the bridge between the keep and nearby Vista
Hill.

===========================================================================
VISTA HILL
===========================================================================

-If you come here, all you'll see is Mario looking at the Keep, then he'll walk
away.  Totally pointless to do.

===========================================================================
MARIO'S PAD
===========================================================================

-After the encounter, go back here and go inside the pipehouse.  Talk to Toad,
and he'll ask where the Princess is.  Then Mario will do one of his (in)famous
no-talk stories.   After that, Toad will suggest going to Mushroom Kingdom to
tell the Chancellor.  Save your game, then attempt to leave.  Toad will come
crashing in, bump you, and take off 1 HP.  Then, he'll give you a Mushroom.
When he asks if you know how to usr items, say yes, because if he goes through
the procedure, you'll waste the Mushroom.  After that lesson, a Goomba will
come in and Toad will ask if you know about Timed Hits.  For the love of God,
say YES!  If you say no, you'll waste 3 FP in the procedure, and you need all
the FP you can get.  After the lessons, Toad will give you 3 Mushrooms, and
head off to Mushroom Way.  Save your game now, as there are no Save Blocks in
Mushroom Way, then follow Toad.

===========================================================================
MUSHROOM WAY
===========================================================================

-Your first real "level".  This mountain pass is full of Goombas, Sky Troopas,
and Spikeys.  There are many battle combinations here.  If you hit a Goomba,
you'll go into battle with either two or three of them.  If you hit a Sky
Troopa, you'll battle one or two of them.  If you touch a Spikey, you'll go
into battle with either two Spikeys or a Spikey and a Sky Troopa.  There are
only two things to worry about in battle:
1) If Mario isn't at least at Level 2, a timed punch will not take out a Sky
Troopa (most of the time).  Use a Jump attack instead.
2) If Mario isn't at least at Level 3, a timed punch will not take out a Spikey
(most of the time).  Don't use Jump attacks, they are useless.
-In the 1st area, Toad is being held by a Goomba.  Defeat the Goomba and Toad
will be so happy he'll give you a Honey Syrup.  In the 2nd area, Toad will get
captured again by a Sky Troopa.  Defeat the Goomba on the spinning flower and
jump onto the right plateau.  Defeat the Sky Troopa and Toad will give you a
Flower Tab.  Before using it, get back on the flower and jump to the left
plateau for a Flower.  Hit the ? Box on the far right side to refill your HP
and FP.  Go into the 3rd room, and defeat enough Spikeys to get to at least
Level 3 or 4.  Gee, what a surprise.  At the end, Toad is captured yet again,

section: this time by a Hammer Brother. Walk up to him twice to go into battle...
text:
this time by a Hammer Brother.  Walk up to him twice to go into battle...
===========================================================================
BOSS: Hammer Brothers
-Hammer Bro (x2): N/A
HP: 50
Defenses: N/A
Weaknesses: Jump

You must beat two of these monsters to get to Mushroom Kingdom.  To beat the
first one, use one timed Jump and one timed punch attack.  After one is dead,
the other one will do Valor Up, doubling his defenses.  For the second one, use
two timed Jumps and one or two timed punches.  Alternate strategy: Get one of
the Hammer Brother's HP very low, then defeat the other one.  Then you can take
out the Valored Up one with about one shot.  You get a Flower Jar and a Hammer
for winning.
===========================================================================
-After the battle, Mario will get his first weapon, a Hammer.  Equip it, and
try it out on the Spikeys in the same room.  After having a little fun, go to
Mushroom Kingdom.

===========================================================================
MUSHROOM KINGDOM
===========================================================================

HIDDEN TREASURE BOXES #1-3

INN: 3 coins
ITEM SHOP:
 _____________________
|Mushroom    | 4 coins|
|---------------------|
|Honey Syrup |10 coins|
|---------------------|
|Pick Me Up  | 5 coins|
|---------------------|
|Able Juice  | 4 coins|
|---------------------|
|Jump Shoes  |30 coins|
|---------------------|
|Antidote Pin|28 coins|
|---------------------|
|Shirt       | 7 coins|
|---------------------|
|Pants       | 7 coins|

-The first town in the game is none other than the famous Mushroom Kingdom.
Don't worry about going into battle.  You can't here, until later. Anyways, go
to the Inn, save your game, then go to the Item Shop and buy a Shirt, some
Pants, a pair of Jump Shoes, an Antidote Pin, and items.  If you don't have
enough money, just at least get the Shirt and Pants.  Now it's time to enter
Mushroom Castle.  Go inside, and follow Toad through thr main hallway and a
small room to the Chancellor's throne room.  As if you didn't know, after all
the talking and story telling, he'll finally get down to business.  First, if
you didn't equip the Hammer, he'll ask you if Toad should tell you.  Say no.
After that, he'll give you a Map and he'll suggest you go down to meet the
Vault Guard.  Go down there and get the 10 coins, flower, and mushroom.  Now,
from the main hallway, go into the left door and up the steps to Toadstool's
room.  To make the maid mad, go between the fireplace and the blue chair and
press A to search.  Search long enough and you'll find Toadstool's ???.  You
probably won't have time to find out what it is, because the maid will yell at
you and give you a Mushroom.  Now, go outside, and try to walk down.
-This scene shows Croco running across the screen, followed by Mallow, our
favorite marshmallow/cloud puff.  After a while, Croco will escape and Mallow
will start crying.  Go up and talk to him, and agree to help him chase Croco.
Now, equip Mallow with the Pants you got and the Antidote Pin (if you have it).
 To get a free Pick Me Up, go into the shop and talk to the shopkeeper.  He'll
give it to you after he's done talking.  Go outside, and talk to the jumping
guy near the eastern exit.  He'll mention that he saw Croco, then Croco will
walk on screen and run right past them.  After the talking is over, exit
through the eastern exit and go to Bandit's Way.

===========================================================================
BANDIT'S WAY
===========================================================================

HIDDEN TREASURE BOX #4

-Don't be surprised if you go into battle a lot here.  Goombas, Spikeys, and
K-9s run amok in this dead-end pass.  Basically, the object is to follow Croco
and trap him enough to go into battle.
-If you every run into a Frogog during battle (and you will), the srategy is
like this: If he's with Spikeys and/or Goombas' have Mario use his hammer and
Mallow do his Thunderbolt attack.  They'll be all gone.
-There is a save block in the lower-left corner of the 1st area.  Hit it, go
into battle with the enemies if you want, and go to the next room.  In the 2nd
room, you need to know how to use the spinning flowers and the rotating
platforms.  Use the flower to jump up to the plateau blocking the path.  To
work the platforms, step on the right-most one.  The left one will rotate 180
degrees and end up right in front of the one you're on.  If you really want to
raise your levels, you can face an unlimited supply of K-9s, thanks to two
caves on opposite plateaus.  Otherwise, use the platforms to get out.  The
second flower isn't needed to get by, but it might be of some use.  The 3rd
room is like the 1st room, just a path with some Goombas and Spikeys.  When you
reach the last fork, go right and beat the K-9, then hit the ? box for a
mushroom, then go back and take the left path to continue.  I love the 4th
room.  After Croco goes away, step on the right-most platform and hit the ? box
right there for a Super Star.  Now run around and hit all the K-9s ASAP.  Don't
worry about running out,
because they will come in through the two passages.  If you want to use the
platforms to get to the other box, it has a Frog Coin in it.  Anyways, go on to
the 5th room.  Looks like you and Croco have found the dead end.  Now he will
hide next to one of the four mini-hills in the middle.  The trick is to sneak
up behind him and press A.  You will need to do this three times.  Don't be
surprised if you go into battle with a Goomba or Sky Troopa.  As I said before,

section: get him three times. Do that, and he'll go into battle...
text:
get him three times.  Do that, and he'll go into battle...
===========================================================================
BOSS: Croco
-Croco: "Ooh!  I'm good!"
HP: 320
Special Defenses: Sleep
Weaknesses: Fire

Croco is actually not that hard to beat.  Mario's Fire Orb is your best bet
here.  He will get "stunned" after the first use, but only after the first
turn.  Mallow's attacks are useless, so either put him in Defense, use
Mushrooms or HP Rain, or use Honey Syrup.  Just before he runs out of HP, he'll
use a Weird Mushroom, restoring 60 HP.  This is an easy battle.  At the end
you'll get a Flower Tab, a Wallet, and Frogfucius's Rare Frog Coin.
===========================================================================
After you get all the stuff, including the Rare Frog Coin, jump on the
trampoline to go back to the save block, then exit and go back to Mushroom
Kingdom.

===========================================================================
MUSHROOM KINGDOM
===========================================================================

-Like I said before, you will go into battle here sometime.  It seems that a
group of Shysters have taken over.  If you're wondering, this isn't Bowser's
fault; it's Smithy's.  The Shysters are easy to beat if Mallow is at least to
Level 4.  Use Thunderbolt to get rid of them.  you will go into battle with
either two or three of those monsters.  There are various items you can gather
here by saving people:
*Defeat the Shyster bugging the mushroom guy near the eastern exit to get 10
coins.
*Defeat the Shyster bugging the guy in the front lawn of the eastern-most
house, then give the guy back his wallet for a Flower Tab.  Come back to him
later in the game for a Frog Coin.
*Defeat the 3 Shysters in the western-most house for a Flower Tab.
*Inside the castle, defeat the Shyster bugging Toad, then the three (or should
it be 4) that are blocking the passage to Toadstool's room, then go inside.
Answer "You bet" to the question to get a Flower Tab (Toadstool's ???, maybe).
*Go into the guest room (right side of castle, room opposite vault) and talk to
the Vault Guard and get a Wake-Up Pin.  Now go into the vault and get the items
again.
-Now you're ready to go into the Chancellor's throne room.  Have your
charatcers at least at Level 6 before going in, because Mario's Super Jump is

super-effective.  Now, to kill Mack...
===========================================================================
BOSS: Mack
-Mack: "Boing, boing, boing."
-Bodyguard (x4): "Boing, boing, boing."
HP: 480/30
Defenses: Mack: Fear, Poison, Sleep, Silence
          Bodyguard: N/A
Weaknesses: Mack: Thunder
            Bodyguard: N/A

Mack is not really that hard, either.  Have Mario and Mallow built up to at
least Level 6.  Have Mario use Super Jump on Mack and Mallow use Thunderbolt on
everybody.  Mack will be "stunned" after Mallow's first Thunderbolt attack.
Have Mario then use Super Jump and Mallow use Thunderbolt or Honey Syrup.  In
other words: Use Super Jump on Mack, Thunderbolt on everybody, and Honey Syrup
if you run out of FP.  You get the first Star Piece when you beat Mack.

section: After beating Mack, you'll get the 1st star piece. After the Chancellor
text:
===========================================================================
After beating Mack, you'll get the 1st star piece.  After the Chancellor
restores order and Mallow suggests going to Tadpole Pond, exit the castle.  Now
go to the shop, and talk to the shopkeeper.  Since you got the coin back,
Mallow can finally get the Cricket Pie for his grandpa.  Now, exit, and go to
the Kero Sewers.

===========================================================================
KERO SEWERS
===========================================================================

-This place is an FAQ writer's nightmare.  Since I have a map of this level, I
can hopefully give you a good explanation of two different paths, the quickest
one and the extended (get all the items) one:
*THE QUICK PATH*
First, enter the level and go through the pipe leading down into the sewers.
Save your game, then jump into the water and swim as far right as you can and
enter that pipe.  Stay along the back wall and go into the pipe on the left
side.  Staying along the right wall, cross the narrow bridge with a Rat Funk on
it, then enter that pipe, which will be the furthest right one.  Go up the
steps and jump on the switch to drain the water.  Go back through the pipe,
then jump down and go into the pipe in the lower-left hand corner and you'll
end up on the upper level of the room with the switch.  Save your game, then
hit the ? box next to it for a mushroom.  Don't worry about the ? box on the
highest ledge.  Go through the pipe on the right side to battle Belome.
*THE EXTENDED PATH*
First, enter the level and go through the pipe leading down into the sewers.
Save your game, then jump into the water and swim as far right as you can and
enter that pipe.  Jump down to the pipe just below where you emerge and enter
that one.  Go to the right and enter that pipe.  Now, go down to the lowest
level, up the steps, and hit the ? box to battle Pandorite.  Use Super Jump a
couple times to beat him.  He'll give you a Flower Jar and a Trueform Pin.
Equip Mario with it.  now, get on the second star from the top, and jump up to
where you dropped down from.  Go to the left to get the flower from the ? box,
then work your way up to the pipe and go in.  Hit the ? box to get a Super
Star, then take out the Rat Funks and the Boo in the upper-right corner, then
enter the pipe in the upper-left corner.  Staying along the back wall, go into
the next pipe.  Staying along the right wall, cross the narrow bridge with a
Rat Funk on it, then enter that pipe, which will be the furthest right one.  Go
up the steps and jump on the switch to drain the water.  Go back through the
pipe,
then jump down and go into the pipe in the lower-left hand corner and you'll
end up on the upper level of the room with the switch.  Save your game, then
hit the ? box next to it for a mushroom.  Don't worry about the ? box on the
highest ledge.  Go through the pipe on the right side to battle Belome.
*Note: I know these directions might be confusing to understand, but you'll get
them after a while.

-Time to get rid of Belome...
===========================================================================
BOSS: Belome
-Belome: "I just... wanna sleep."
HP: 500
Special Defenses: Sleep
Weaknesses: Thunder

You will meet Belome twice in the game, once here and again in Belome's Temple,
between Land's End and Monstro Town.  If you don't have a Trueform Pin on
Mario, Mallow gets eaten, and you're out of FP, you'll hate this battle
(there's a 90% chance that won't happen).  Anyways, have Mario use Super Jump
and Mallow use Thunderbolt.  Belome does have sleep attacks, so be careful.  He
will attempt to do S'Crow Funk on Mario, and might even EAT Mallow.  Just keep
attacking and restoring and Belome is history, for now.  In fact, you don't
even get anything for beating him, except a free trip down the Midas River

(whooptydoo).
===========================================================================
After the battle, you'll be able to attempt the Midas River course.

===========================================================================
MIDAS RIVER
===========================================================================

-Since this whole level is a mini-game, see the Mini-Games section.
-At the end of this 1st ride, the mushroom guy will give you a Nok Nok Shell as
a new weapon.  It works.

===========================================================================
TADPOLE POND
===========================================================================

(To find both shops, first introduce yourself to Frogfucius, then go to the
furthest left beachland you can.)

-When you enter, you will not be able to talk to any of the tadpoles.  Go
straight up to the small switch/rock and a tadpole will appear.  Mallow will
come out and start a conversation.  When they ask about your jumping ability
jump.  After that, then Mallow's grandfather, Frogfucius, will float on screen,
being carried by a Lakitu.  After many miscommunications and words exchanged,
Frogfucius will tell the tadpoles to make a brid ge to his "home".  Now you can
talk to any of the tadpoles you want.  To get an Alto Card for the juice bar,
go all the way right and into Melody Bay and play Frogfucius's Suite #18 (see
Mini-Games section).  When that's done, go to the juice bar and buy some
Elixirs, then cross the tadpole bridge.  Basically, Frogfucius will give you a
recap of the game from Bowser's Keep to the star piece.  He will also mention
that Toadstool isn't at the Keep anymore.  If you payed attention, don't agree
to a recap of the recap.  After that, Mallow will be in for a big shock, as
Frogfucius tells Mallow he's not his real grandfather and that Mallow's not a
tadpole.  Frogfucius suggests that Mallow follow Mario on his adventure.  After
that's done, go up and talk to him.  If you have the Cricket Pie, he'll give
you the Froggie Stick, Mallow's first weapon.  Equip it, save your game at
Melody
Bay, and go onwards to Rose Way.

===========================================================================
ROSE WAY
===========================================================================

-This stage is very different.  The main part of the stage is to navigate the
moving platforms across the lakes to reach each island.  you can find a
boatload of coins, plus a flower and a mushroom.
-If you go into the upper-left passage, you can get a tricky frog coin.  To get
to it, defeat the Shy Guy on the platform, then jump to it.  From that one,
jump onto the next Shy Guy and beat it.  Now comes the hard part.  You must now
jump from the first platform to the second platform, then from the second
platform up to the treasure box.  It's not really worth the effort, but you can
go for it.
-If you go into the upper-right passage, you can access a good room to get
stuff.  First, beat the two Crooks to get mucho cash.  Then attack the Shy Guy
haaging from the Lakitu.  If you defeat four of them, Lakitu will give in and
throw a mushroom, which will restore your HP and FP.
-The goal is to get out through the lower-right passage.  In that room is the
best treasure trove in the game. Wipe out the Crooks, then go for the chests.
They hold a total of 20 coins and a mushroom restoring your HP and FP.  When
you hit a chest, a Shy Guy comes down.  You can get good experience and coins
from them.  The best part is, if you go off screen, and come back in, all the
chests refill and Shy Guys reappear.  Sorry, but the Crooks only reappear when
you leave the stage and reenter.
-In the last room you'll see Bowser with his Koopa Troop.  After they leave,
you can go by and enter Rose Town.

===========================================================================
ROSE TOWN
===========================================================================

HIDDEN TREASURE BOXES #5-6

INN: Free (when you return)
ITEM SHOP:
(left counter)
 ____________________
|Mushroom   | 4 coins|
|--------------------|
